title: Adjective Declension 2: Accusative Singular and the Animacy Split
titleRussian: Склонение прилагательных 2: винительный падеж и одушевлённость
description: The accusative singular for hard-stem adjectives. The masculine inanimate keeps the nominative form (-ый). The masculine animate borrows the genitive form (-ого). The feminine has its own ending (-ую). The neuter is always like the nominative (-ое).
descriptionRussian: Винительный падеж единственного числа: мужской неодушевлённый как именительный (-ый), мужской одушевлённый как родительный (-ого), женский -ую, средний как именительный (-ое).
intro: The accusative brings back the animacy split you met in the A1 accusative book, and it works the same way: masculine words for people and animals borrow their form from the genitive, while masculine words for things stay as they are. What is new is only that the adjective has to do it too, in step with its noun.
rules: Masculine inanimate (objects, places, abstractions): the adjective in the accusative is identical to the nominative. -ый stays -ый. Я читаю новый журнал.
Masculine animate (people, animals): the adjective borrows the GENITIVE form. -ый becomes -ого. Я знаю нового брата. (The same -ого reappears as the genitive in Lesson 3.)
Feminine (-а, -я, or -ь noun): the adjective takes -ую in the accusative. -ая becomes -ую. Я читаю новую книгу. Animacy makes no difference for the feminine.
Neuter: the adjective is identical to the nominative. -ое stays -ое. Я читаю новое письмо.
The animacy split applies only to the masculine in the singular. The plural will keep its own animacy split (Lesson 7), but feminine and neuter singulars ignore it.
examples: Я читаю новый журнал. (I am reading a new magazine.) Журнал is masculine inanimate, so the adjective stays -ый: новый.
Я знаю нового брата Маши. (I know Masha's new brother.) Брат is masculine animate, so the adjective takes -ого: нового.
Я читаю новую книгу. (I am reading a new book.) Книга is feminine, so the adjective takes -ую: новую.
Я люблю старое озеро. (I love the old lake.) Озеро is neuter, so the adjective stays -ое: старое.
Антон видит красивую улицу. (Anton sees a beautiful street.) Улица is feminine inanimate, but feminine ignores animacy: -ую → красивую.
Маша знает старого учителя. (Masha knows the old teacher.) Учитель is masculine animate, so the adjective takes -ого: старого.

items.hint: Lesson 1 recap: which slot is the nominative for книга?
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 1. Книга is feminine singular. In the nominative the hard-stem feminine ending is -ая: новая. Today's drill, which starts at Q1.2, switches to the accusative.

items.promptEnglish: I am reading a new magazine.
items.hint: Журнал is masculine inanimate. What does the adjective do in the accusative?
items.explanation: Журнал is masculine inanimate. For masculine inanimate, the accusative adjective is identical to the nominative: -ый stays -ый. So новый.

items.hint: Брат is masculine animate. The adjective borrows which case's form?
items.explanation: Брат is masculine animate. For masculine animate, the accusative adjective borrows the genitive form: -ый becomes -ого. So нового. Lesson 3 will teach -ого officially as the genitive ending; today it shows up here as the animate-accusative borrowing.

items.promptEnglish: Anton is reading an interesting book.
items.hint: Книгу is feminine. The feminine accusative ending is brand new today.
items.explanation: Книгу is feminine accusative. The feminine adjective ending in the accusative is -ую: интересную. Notice both the noun (-у) and the adjective (-ую) shift in parallel: nominative книга → accusative книгу; nominative интересная → accusative интересную.

items.hint: Озеро is neuter. Does the adjective change in the accusative?
items.explanation: Озеро is neuter. The neuter accusative is identical to the nominative: -ое stays -ое. So старое. The same form would appear as the subject of a sentence: 'Старое озеро красивое' would also start with старое.

items.hint: Друг is masculine animate. Recall the rule from Q1.3.
items.explanation: Друг is masculine animate. The adjective borrows the genitive form: -ый becomes -ого. So старого. Pattern check: Q1.3 had нового брата; this is the same rule on a different animate noun.

blanks: Маша покупает _____ машину. (Masha buys a beautiful car.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Машину is feminine accusative. The feminine adjective ending in the accusative is -ую: красивую. The same -ую appears on every feminine accusative adjective regardless of animacy.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: In the evening Masha reads a beautiful book.
errorCorrection.explanation: Книгу is feminine in the accusative (the noun has already shifted from книга to книгу), so the adjective takes the feminine accusative ending -ую: красивую. Красивая is the nominative form, correct only when the book is the subject.

errorCorrection.sentence: Маша хорошо знает умный брата Лены.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha knows Lena's smart brother well.
errorCorrection.explanation: Брат is masculine animate, and a masculine animate noun in the accusative borrows the genitive form on both the noun (брата) and the adjective: -ый becomes -ого, giving умного. Умный is the nominative, the form for a subject.

errorCorrection.sentence: Антон покупает старого журнал в киоске.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton buys an old magazine at the kiosk.
errorCorrection.explanation: Журнал is masculine inanimate, so its accusative is identical to the nominative on both noun and adjective: старый журнал stays unchanged. Старого is the masculine ANIMATE accusative (старого брата), which fires only for living beings.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I am reading a new magazine.
minimalPairs.explanation: Журнал is masculine INANIMATE, so the accusative adjective is identical to the nominative: -ый. Нового would be required if the noun were animate (e.g., нового брата).
Учитель is masculine ANIMATE, so the accusative adjective borrows the genitive form: -ого. Старый would be the form for a masculine inanimate noun like учебник.

reviewVocab.definition: accusative case (marks the direct object; answers 'Кого? / Что?')
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Я знаю нового брата' слово 'брата' и слово 'нового' стоят в винительном падеже.

reviewVocab.definition: animate (a person or animal; in masculine singular accusative, the adjective borrows the genitive ending -ого)
reviewVocab.example: Слово 'друг' одушевлённое, поэтому винительный падеж выглядит как родительный: старого друга.

reviewVocab.definition: inanimate (a thing, place, or abstraction; in masculine singular accusative, the adjective is identical to the nominative)
reviewVocab.example: Слово 'журнал' неодушевлённое, поэтому винительный падеж совпадает с именительным: новый журнал.
